events.title: The election of Pope Francis
events.shortBlurb: The cardinals chose Jorge Mario Bergoglio of Buenos Aires, the first pope from the Americas and the first Jesuit…
body: On 28 February 2013 Benedict XVI resigned the papacy, the first pope to do so in nearly six hundred years. The conclave that opened on 12 March needed only five ballots: the next evening, 13 March, white smoke rose over the Sistine Chapel, and Cardinal Jean-Louis Tauran announced the election of Jorge Mario Bergoglio, archbishop of Buenos Aires, as the 266th pope, taking the name Francis after Francis of Assisi.

Born in Buenos Aires on 17 December 1936 to a family of Italian immigrants, he was the first Jesuit to sit in Peter's chair, the first pope from the Americas and the Southern Hemisphere, and the first from outside Europe in more than twelve hundred years, since the Syrian Gregory III, who died in 741.

From the balcony he greeted Rome and the world simply, bowed his head, and asked the silent crowd to pray for him before he gave them his blessing. The simplicity of that first night, joined to his chosen name, set the note of poverty and mercy that would mark his pontificate.
